candidates: When a code change converts an implicit runtime crash (e.g., a TypeError from an out-of-bounds access) into an explicit `throw new Error(...)`, verify that the test suite includes a test that asserts the specific error is thrown—not just that no crash occurs.
Prefer template literals over string concatenation for building strings in both source and test files; flag any new or modified code that still uses `+` to assemble strings.

Error messages for invalid-input conditions (e.g., out-of-bounds indices, missing required values) should include the actual offending value and the valid range or constraint so the message is immediately actionable without users having to inspect source code.

In Jest tests, `.toThrow()` must be chained on the `expect()` call itself, not on the return value of the function under test. The correct pattern is `expect(() => fn()).toThrow(message)`; placing `.toThrow()` inside the arrow function (e.g., `expect(() => fn().toThrow(message))`) silently turns the assertion into a no-op. Flag any test where `.toThrow()` appears inside the `expect(() => ...)` callback.
